headline: High: broad network-egress CRM agent paired with document-ingesting support RAG creates default leakage and cascading-action risk; prompt-injection is lower but present via shared content flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest and act on content via MCP/direct function calls, and kotaemon processes documents, HTML, chat transcripts, and citations. If kotaemon output is copied into aci workflows or a shared workspace, attacker-controlled text can steer aci. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF kotaemon output is routed into aci prompts or MCP inputs
IF either agent reads shared files without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of generated text into aci
Add a manual review step before copying outputs
Tag untrusted documents and strip instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data while kotaemon handles documents and API keys. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive content can flow from one agent into the other's outbound API calls. The profiles do not prove isolation, so the safer medium rating applies.
conditions: IF the two agents share files, credentials, or a common operator account
IF sensitive CRM or document data is opened in kotaemon and then forwarded by aci
mitigations: Use separate API keys per agent
Keep distinct directories for each agent
Block outbound access except to approved endpoints
Rotate any shared secrets before co-running
requires-engineering: enforce workspace and credential isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both profiles support multiple instances and both have broad network egress, so concurrent writes or API actions can collide on shared mutable resources such as CRM records, email threads, or document stores. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, and uncertainty about shared backends means conflict risk is real in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same CRM, mailbox, or document repository
IF no external lock or queue serializes their writes
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource ownership
Serialize writes through one queue
Pause one agent during bulk updates
Review duplicate-write logs daily
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can act on CRM, email, calendar, and support systems, while kotaemon produces extracted document content, citations, and chat transcripts that may be treated as authoritative. If kotaemon output is fed into aci without verification, aci can execute incorrect downstream actions. That default action-taking pathway makes the blast radius potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF kotaemon summaries or citations are used as authoritative input to aci
IF aci is allowed to send emails or update CRM records from those inputs
mitigations: Require human approval before external actions
Cross-check extracted facts against source documents
Limit aci to draft-only mode
Log source-to-action traceability
requires-engineering: add verification gates before side effects

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, calendar, and support data, while kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, but both clearly process regulated personal and secret-bearing data. Because compliance gaps are plausible and not mitigated by default, medium is warranted rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer data or secrets are processed in either agent
IF retention, deletion, or residency policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Inventory data classes before deployment
Keep regulated data out of kotaemon where possible
Set short retention windows
Document deletion/export procedures
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
